eras.name: The revival · Rutger Fick and Claude

milestones.title: First commit
milestones.text: Demian Wassermann starts the repository with restricted-diffusion code extracted from the Athena team's tools (Callaghan, Gaussian phase, multiple correlation function). Its first name is microstruktur.

milestones.title: Watson & Bingham
milestones.text: Analytic Watson (4 April) and Bingham (7 April) orientation distributions let sticks and zeppelins fan out, so a model can say how dispersed the axons are.

milestones.title: Ball & stick
milestones.text: The ball-and-stick model: an isotropic ball for free water and a stick for the axons, the stick having arrived on 5 April. Its tutorial example follows in June.

milestones.title: MIX optimisation
milestones.text: A global fitter that solves the volume fractions linearly and searches the other parameters, for models a local fit gets lost in.

milestones.title: Named dmipy
milestones.text: microstruktur becomes mipy on 7 January, and dmipy on 31 January.

milestones.title: Release 0.1
milestones.text: The first release: an open-source framework for reproducible diffusion MRI microstructure research.

milestones.title: CSD, any kernel
milestones.text: Constrained spherical deconvolution with any multi-compartment model as its kernel, multi-tissue and multi-shell.

milestones.title: 1.0 + the paper
milestones.text: The stable 1.0 release, and on the same day the toolbox paper in Frontiers in Neuroinformatics 13:64, by Rutger Fick, Demian Wassermann and Rachid Deriche.

milestones.title: AMICO joins
milestones.text: A community contribution by Sara Sedlar: AMICO, fast linear fitting over a dictionary of model signals.

milestones.title: Kept alive
milestones.text: Through the quiet years the users keep it working: PyPI packaging in 2021, CSD+ in 2022 and a fix for newer Python versions in 2024, all from the community.

milestones.title: The revival
milestones.text: dmipy is revived in private development repositories, now archived, as a collaboration between Rutger Fick and Claude, Anthropic's AI. From here on, a researcher and an AI build it together.

milestones.title: Watson & Bingham, again
milestones.label: W & B, again
milestones.text: The first work of the collaboration (Claude Sonnet 4.6), in dmipy-fit: Watson- and Bingham-dispersed models on JAX on 7 April, then their exact analytical spherical harmonics on 28 April. They ship publicly in dmipy-fit 2.0.

milestones.title: dmrai-lab.org
milestones.text: The lab's website goes up, with its manifesto: physics is the specification.

milestones.title: 2.0: two engines
milestones.text: dmipy is rebuilt from the ground up as two engines that check each other: dmipy-sim, a new Monte-Carlo simulator, and dmipy-fit, the original's model fitting on JAX and GPU. Its home is dmipy.org.

milestones.title: Two observables
milestones.text: The revival's first paper: surface relaxivity and diffusion read the same wall collisions, which can bias the intra-axonal fraction and the myelin water fraction.

milestones.title: Meshes
milestones.text: Real cell shapes as substrates: triangular meshes from PLY files, 3-D periodic, walked with the same physics as cylinders and spheres.

milestones.title: Design joins
milestones.text: Diffusion waveforms a real scanner can play (LTE, PTE, STE, OGSE and stimulated echoes) under its hardware limits, building on NOW (Sjölund et al. 2015), and exported to Pulseq.

milestones.title: MT + vector Bloch
milestones.text: Magnetization transfer enters the walk: a bound proton pool exchanging with free water, and a vector-Bloch engine that follows the RF pulses themselves.

milestones.title: The .rpk spec
milestones.text: An open, code-free format for a Monte-Carlo walk kept once and replayed for any acquisition: the Replay Pack specification, published as a draft for comment.

milestones.title: Matrix method
milestones.text: Exact restricted diffusion in planes, cylinders and spheres for any gradient waveform (the matrix method of Callaghan and Grebenkov), as compartments a fit can use.

milestones.title: Replay packs
milestones.text: Walk once, keep the walk, and replay any gradient waveform from it. The same day, dmipy-fit fits through packs and dmipy-design designs waveforms through them.

milestones.title: Myelin's field
milestones.text: Susceptibility on meshes: the magnetic field of a myelin sheath, computed from the mesh and sampled along every walker's path.

milestones.title: Substrates = specs
milestones.text: Every substrate becomes a specification, data rather than code: pools, walls and seeds, checked before a walk starts. CATERPillar and DiSCo enter the same way.

milestones.title: One acquisition
milestones.text: One acquisition object, ScannerSequence, for simulation, fitting and design alike: what the scanner plays, from excitation to readout.

milestones.title: Replay phantoms
milestones.text: Images from packs: voxels composed from replay packs and free water, so a whole phantom is replayed rather than simulated.

milestones.title: A brain, replayed
milestones.text: A real brain, the BATMAN tutorial subject, rebuilt from its MRtrix result as a replay phantom in the bore. Its page on dmipy.org replays it in the browser.

milestones.title: DiSCo, every tier
milestones.text: DiSCo, the Monte-Carlo tractography phantom of Rafael-Patino et al., as a specification: one walk that carries the diffusion, the wall contact and the myelin's field together.

milestones.title: Scanner as a model
milestones.text: The scanner itself becomes a forward model, with its field shape, gradient nonlinearity and concomitant fields, starting with the 64 mT Hyperfine Swoop.

milestones.title: DiSCo Space
milestones.text: The DiSCo phantom as a public Hugging Face Space: choose an acquisition, replay every voxel, reconstruct and track.

milestones.title: FOD tracker
milestones.text: Streamline tractography on fibre-orientation fields: one batched tracker on the GPU, following dipy's conventions.

milestones.title: The step law
milestones.text: The walk's step is certified, not tuned: a Gauss pair of step lengths, sized for a stated tolerance on the diffusion spectrum.

milestones.title: 600 pores
milestones.text: Open replay packs of 600 canonical pores (planes, cylinders and spheres from 0.1 to 20 µm), each certified for any waveform of its scanner class.

milestones.title: CACTUS axons
milestones.text: A CACTUS bundle of 176 myelinated axons, and the same axons walked by MC/DC and MCMRSimulator.jl, read by the same reader.

milestones.title: Reference walks
milestones.text: A slab split by a membrane, checked against the exact one-dimensional Bloch–Torrey solution, and float coefficient walks, the unrounded walks a pack's encoding is measured against.

milestones.title: DiSCo replayed
milestones.text: DiSCo as one replay pack: 12,196 strands and 321 million walkers, every tier stored, certified for any acquisition of its scanner class.

milestones.title: NumPy reader
milestones.text: Replay packs read and replayed with NumPy alone, with no walk and no GPU. dmipy-replay's first release on PyPI.

milestones.title: Replayable Monte Carlo MRI: the replay preprint (arXiv:2611.01758)
milestones.label: Replay preprint
milestones.text: Replayable Monte Carlo MRI: From Persistent Tissue Microphysics to Queryable Virtual Phantoms. Walker histories are kept as replay packs, up to 5000 times smaller, so any acquisition becomes a cheap query of the same walk. The DiSCo Space is its demo.

milestones.title: Other engines
milestones.text: Walks from other simulators become replay packs too, so different engines are compared through one reader.

milestones.title: The envelope
milestones.text: Every pack states its guarantee in physical terms: a band, a gradient amplitude, field and tissue bounds. A request outside it is refused by name.

milestones.title: dmipy 3.0
milestones.text: One pip install for the family: dmipy-sim, dmipy-replay, dmipy-fit and dmipy-design, with dmipy-analytic under them and dmipy-tract as an extra.

milestones.title: Closed forms, once
milestones.text: The closed-form signals of special cases, each with its assumptions and its source, kept in one place and imported by every package. Watson and Bingham are among them.

milestones.title: Lossless codec
milestones.text: A lossless band codec (bitshuffle and zlib): the same integers, bit-transposed and deflated, so packs shrink and not one decoded value changes.
